canonical_record.label: JUNO 207-day atmospheric mass-splitting fits
canonical_record.summary: The September 2026 JUNO analysis reported 8,294 inverse-beta-decay candidates in 207.2 live days at an average 52.5 km reactor baseline and obtained different fitted atmospheric mass splittings under normal and inverted ordering using a Daya Bay constraint.

sources.title: Measurement of Neutrino Oscillation Parameters at JUNO and Indication of the Neutrino Mass Ordering

statement: The September 2026 JUNO analysis reported 8,294 inverse-beta-decay candidates in 207.2 live days at an average 52.5 km reactor baseline and obtained different fitted atmospheric mass splittings under normal and inverted ordering using a Daya Bay constraint.

scope.time: 207.2 live days, as reported in September 2026
scope.assumptions: The fitted atmospheric splitting is conditional on the chosen mass ordering and external Daya Bay constraint; the sample is not an independent determination of ordering.
scope.uncertainty: Oscillation-parameter fits and event counts do not establish the absolute neutrino mass or conclusive ordering.

support.quote: The analysis is based on 207.2 live days of data, comprising 8,294 inverse beta-decay candidates collected at an average reactor baseline of 52.5 km. A world-leading precision of approximately 1% was achieved for the atmospheric neutrino mass splitting $\Delta m^2_{31}$, with $\Delta m^2_{31}=+2.509^{+0.027}_{-0.025}\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{eV}^2$ for normal ordering and $\Delta m^2_{31}=-2.482^{+0.025}_{-0.026}\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{eV}^2$ for inverted ordering, using the Daya Bay constraint in the fit to resolve the correct physical minimum under each mass-ordering hypothesis.

canonical_record.label: JUNO solar oscillation-parameter estimates
canonical_record.summary: The September 2026 JUNO analysis reported sin²θ12=0.3036±0.0064 and Δm21²=(7.388±0.078)×10^-5 eV², with stated relative precisions of 2.1% and 1.1%, respectively.

sources.title: Measurement of Neutrino Oscillation Parameters at JUNO and Indication of the Neutrino Mass Ordering

statement: The September 2026 JUNO analysis reported sin²θ12=0.3036±0.0064 and Δm21²=(7.388±0.078)×10^-5 eV², with stated relative precisions of 2.1% and 1.1%, respectively.

scope.assumptions: Oscillation parameters are fitted within the model used by the collaboration; relative precision is as reported in the abstract.
scope.uncertainty: These are not absolute neutrino-mass estimates, and the reported uncertainties should not be recast as independently validated accuracy.

support.quote: We further improved the world's most precise measurements of the solar oscillation parameters, obtaining $\sin^2\theta_{12}=0.3036\pm0.0064$ and $\Delta m^2_{21}=(7.388\pm0.078)\times10^{-5}\,\mathrm{eV}^2$, corresponding to relative precisions of 2.1% and 1.1%, respectively.

canonical_record.label: JUNO combined ordering indication and Bayes factor
canonical_record.summary: The September 2026 JUNO collaboration reported that incorporating long-baseline accelerator constraints on Δm31² favored normal over inverted neutrino mass ordering with one-sided significance of at least 2.1σ across CP-violating phases and a Bayesian Bayes factor of 10.18.

sources.title: Measurement of Neutrino Oscillation Parameters at JUNO and Indication of the Neutrino Mass Ordering

statement: The September 2026 JUNO collaboration reported that incorporating long-baseline accelerator constraints on Δm31² favored normal over inverted neutrino mass ordering with one-sided significance of at least 2.1σ across CP-violating phases and a Bayesian Bayes factor of 10.18.

scope.population: JUNO reactor data combined with external long-baseline accelerator constraints
scope.assumptions: Frequentist significance and Bayesian evidence reflect different inferential procedures and the cited combination; these are not reactor-only results.
scope.uncertainty: An indication is not a definitive ordering determination; the Bayes factor depends on likelihood/prior choices not detailed in the retained abstract.

support.quote: Incorporating constraints on $\Delta m^2_{31}$ from long-baseline accelerator neutrino experiments into our analysis favored normal ordering over inverted ordering, with a one-sided significance of at least $2.1\sigma$ across all possible CP-violating phases; a Bayesian analysis yielded a Bayes factor of 10.18 in favor of normal ordering.

canonical_record.label: KATRIN effective electron-antineutrino mass bound
canonical_record.summary: KATRIN reported a fitted squared effective electron-antineutrino mass of -0.14 (+0.13/-0.15) eV² from five tritium beta-decay campaigns and an effective-mass upper limit of 0.45 eV at 90% confidence using 259 measurement days and 36 million electrons.

sources.title: Direct neutrino-mass measurement based on 259 days of KATRIN data

statement: KATRIN reported a fitted squared effective electron-antineutrino mass of -0.14 (+0.13/-0.15) eV² from five tritium beta-decay campaigns and an effective-mass upper limit of 0.45 eV at 90% confidence using 259 measurement days and 36 million electrons.

scope.time: First five neutrino-mass campaigns totaling 259 measurement days; report submitted 2024 and published 2025
scope.assumptions: A negative unconstrained best-fit squared-mass parameter is a statistical fit result, not a physical negative neutrino mass; effective kinematic mass differs from the cosmological sum.
scope.uncertainty: No positive absolute-mass measurement follows from the upper limit; systematics/background modeled in analysis and not fully auditable from captured abstract.
scope.units: eV²; eV; electrons; days; confidence level
scope.quantifiers: best-fit mν²=-0.14 (+0.13/-0.15) eV²; mν<0.45 eV at 90% CL; 36 million electrons

support.quote: Based on the first five neutrino-mass measurement campaigns, we derive a best-fit value of $m_\nu^{2} = {-0.14^{+0.13}_{-0.15}}~\mathrm{eV^2}$, resulting in an upper limit of $m_\nu < {0.45}~\mathrm{eV}$ at 90 % confidence level. With six times the statistics of previous data sets, amounting to 36 million electrons collected in 259 measurement days, a substantial reduction of the background level and improved systematic uncertainties, this result tightens KATRIN's previous bound by a factor of almost two.

canonical_record.label: KamLAND-Zen xenon-136 neutrinoless-decay half-life limit
canonical_record.summary: The KamLAND-Zen full-dataset search with 745 kg enriched xenon and 2.1 tonne-years of xenon-136 exposure, combined with its previous phase, reported a 90%-confidence lower bound on the neutrinoless double-beta half-life of 3.8×10^26 years.

sources.title: Search for Majorana Neutrinos with the Complete KamLAND-Zen Dataset

statement: The KamLAND-Zen full-dataset search with 745 kg enriched xenon and 2.1 tonne-years of xenon-136 exposure, combined with its previous phase, reported a 90%-confidence lower bound on the neutrinoless double-beta half-life of 3.8×10^26 years.

scope.population: KamLAND-Zen 800 xenon-136 data and preceding KamLAND-Zen phase
scope.time: Full dataset in arXiv report first submitted 2024, revised 2026
scope.assumptions: The exposure is from KamLAND-Zen 800; the half-life limit uses a combination with the previous phase rather than just that exposure.
scope.uncertainty: A nondetection bounds the assumed decay channel; it does not demonstrate zero neutrino mass or Dirac nature.
scope.units: kg enriched Xe; tonne-years ^136Xe; years; 90% CL
scope.quantifiers: 745 kg enriched xenon; 2.1 tonne-years Xe-136; T1/2^0ν >3.8×10^26 yr (90% CL)

support.quote:
We present a search for neutrinoless double-beta ($0
u eta eta$) decay of $^{136}$Xe using the full \mbox{KamLAND-Zen 800} dataset with 745\,kg of enriched xenon, corresponding to an exposure of $2.1$\,ton\,yr of $^{136}$Xe. This updated search benefits from a more than twofold increase in exposure, recovery of photo-sensor gain, and reduced background from muon-induced spallation of xenon. Combining with the search in the previous KamLAND-Zen phase, we obtain a lower limit for the $0
u eta eta$ decay half-life of $T_{1/2}^{0
u} > 3.8 	imes 10^{26}$\,yr at 90\% C.L., a factor of 1.7 improvement over the previous limit.

canonical_record.label: KamLAND-Zen nuclear-model-dependent effective Majorana bound
canonical_record.summary: The KamLAND-Zen full-dataset report translated its neutrinoless xenon-136 double-beta half-life constraint into effective Majorana neutrino-mass upper limits ranging from 28 to 122 meV using phenomenological nuclear matrix-element calculations.

sources.title: Search for Majorana Neutrinos with the Complete KamLAND-Zen Dataset

statement: The KamLAND-Zen full-dataset report translated its neutrinoless xenon-136 double-beta half-life constraint into effective Majorana neutrino-mass upper limits ranging from 28 to 122 meV using phenomenological nuclear matrix-element calculations.

scope.population: KamLAND-Zen xenon-136 neutrinoless double-beta decay interpretation
scope.time: Abstract of 2024 submission, as revised March 2026
scope.assumptions: Translation assumes a neutrinoless-decay interpretation and chosen nuclear matrix elements; it is not direct kinematic neutrino-mass spectroscopy.
scope.uncertainty: The mass range varies by nuclear modeling; nondetection does not establish whether neutrinos are Majorana or Dirac.

support.quote: The corresponding upper limits on the effective Majorana neutrino mass are in the range 28--122\,meV using phenomenological nuclear matrix element calculations.

canonical_record.label: Planck 2018 plus BAO neutrino mass-sum bound
canonical_record.summary: The Planck 2018 cosmological-parameter analysis reported Σmν<0.12 eV as a 95% upper limit when combined with baryon acoustic oscillation data in its base spatially flat ΛCDM framework.

statement: The Planck 2018 cosmological-parameter analysis reported Σmν<0.12 eV as a 95% upper limit when combined with baryon acoustic oscillation data in its base spatially flat ΛCDM framework.

scope.population: Cosmological Planck CMB constraints combined with BAO
scope.time: Planck 2018 results, abstract of version revised August 2021
scope.assumptions: Cosmological mass-sum inference assumes base ΛCDM and a specified CMB-plus-BAO data combination; upper limits are quoted at 95%.
scope.uncertainty: Cannot be interpreted as a direct laboratory neutrino-mass measurement or model-independent limit.

support.quote: Combining with BAO we constrain the effective extra relativistic degrees of freedom to be $N_{\rm eff} = 2.99\pm 0.17$, and the neutrino mass is tightly constrained to $\sum m_\nu< 0.12$eV.

canonical_record.label: DESI DR2 neutrino sum bound changes with dark-energy model
canonical_record.summary: The DESI DR2 analysis reported a 95% upper limit Σmν<0.064 eV for DESI BAO plus CMB under ΛCDM, versus Σmν<0.16 eV under a time-evolving w0wa dark-energy model using the same stated combination.

sources.title: DESI DR2 Results II: Measurements of Baryon Acoustic Oscillations and Cosmological Constraints

statement: The DESI DR2 analysis reported a 95% upper limit Σmν<0.064 eV for DESI BAO plus CMB under ΛCDM, versus Σmν<0.16 eV under a time-evolving w0wa dark-energy model using the same stated combination.

scope.population: DESI DR2 BAO and external CMB combination
scope.assumptions: The two limits are conditional on alternative cosmological dark-energy parametrizations; not BAO-only data.
scope.uncertainty: Neither 95% upper limit is a direct mass observation or a universal model-independent upper bound.

support.quote: From the combination of DESI and CMB we derive 95% upper limits on the sum of neutrino masses, finding $\sum m_\nu<0.064$ eV assuming $\Lambda$CDM and $\sum m_\nu<0.16$ eV in the $w_0w_a$ model.

canonical_record.label: DESI DR2 neutrino mass tension and boundary-sensitive inference
canonical_record.summary: The DESI DR2 neutrino-constraints analysis reported a Feldman-Cousins 95% bound Σmν<0.053 eV after correcting for the zero-mass boundary, below the oscillation-inferred lower limit, and a separate effective-mass parametrization yielding 3σ tension under its analysis assumptions.

sources.title: Constraints on Neutrino Physics from DESI DR2 BAO and DR1 Full Shape

statement: The DESI DR2 neutrino-constraints analysis reported a Feldman-Cousins 95% bound Σmν<0.053 eV after correcting for the zero-mass boundary, below the oscillation-inferred lower limit, and a separate effective-mass parametrization yielding 3σ tension under its analysis assumptions.

scope.population: DESI DR2 BAO combined with external Planck and ACT CMB datasets as analyzed in this study
scope.assumptions: Feldman-Cousins and Bayesian effective-parameter results are distinct statistical constructions; effective negative density is an analysis device, not physical negative neutrino mass.
scope.uncertainty: Claimed tension depends on model assumptions, priors and treatment of boundaries; source itself mentions possible systematics and evolving dark energy.

support.quote: However, we determine using frequentist and Bayesian methods that our constraints are in tension with the lower limits derived from neutrino oscillations. Correcting for the physical boundary at zero mass, we report a 95% Feldman-Cousins upper limit of $\sum m_\nu<0.053$ eV, breaching the lower limit from neutrino oscillations. Considering a more general Bayesian analysis with an effective cosmological neutrino mass parameter, $\sum m_{\nu,\rm{eff}}$, that allows for negative energy densities and removes unsatisfactory prior weight effects, we derive constraints that are in $3\sigma$ tension with the same oscillation limit.

canonical_record.label: Planck 2018 BAO mass bounds change under hierarchy priors
canonical_record.summary: A Bayesian reanalysis using Planck 2018 CMB plus BOSS DR12, MGS and 6dFGS BAO data reported 95%-confidence neutrino mass-sum limits of 0.12 eV (degenerate masses), 0.15 eV (normal ordering) and 0.17 eV (inverted ordering), attributing their differences to mass-sum priors.

sources.title: Updated results on neutrino mass and mass hierarchy from cosmology with Planck 2018 likelihoods

statement: A Bayesian reanalysis using Planck 2018 CMB plus BOSS DR12, MGS and 6dFGS BAO data reported 95%-confidence neutrino mass-sum limits of 0.12 eV (degenerate masses), 0.15 eV (normal ordering) and 0.17 eV (inverted ordering), attributing their differences to mass-sum priors.

scope.population: Cosmological reanalysis of Planck 2018 and specified BAO surveys
scope.assumptions: Mass hierarchy scenarios impose different mass-sum prior distributions; this is reanalysis, not new independent Planck data.
scope.uncertainty: Values depend on chosen cosmological model and priors, not proof of a mass ordering or inconsistency.

canonical_record.label: DESI and CMB neutrino constraints with isocurvature allowed
canonical_record.summary: A 2026 joint CMB, DESI DR2 and supernova analysis reported that allowing a neutrino-density isocurvature mode shifted its 95% neutrino mass-sum limits from 0.052 to 0.057 eV under ΛCDM and 0.111 to 0.115 eV under dynamical dark energy, without detecting the isocurvature mode.

sources.title: Constraints on the Sum of Neutrino Masses from ACT DR6 and DESI DR2 Considering Isocurvature Initial Conditions

statement: A 2026 joint CMB, DESI DR2 and supernova analysis reported that allowing a neutrino-density isocurvature mode shifted its 95% neutrino mass-sum limits from 0.052 to 0.057 eV under ΛCDM and 0.111 to 0.115 eV under dynamical dark energy, without detecting the isocurvature mode.

scope.population: Joint Planck 2018, ACT DR6, SPT-3G CMB; DESI DR2 BAO; DES Year 5 supernovae
scope.time: 2026 paper under two cosmological model assumptions
scope.assumptions: The comparison changes initial-condition assumptions within each dark-energy model; these are model/prior-dependent posterior limits.
scope.uncertainty: The sub-oscillation-minimum ΛCDM bound can arise from a prior extending to zero and is not a model-independent exclusion of normal ordering.

support.quote: Within the $\Lambda$CDM model, the 95\% upper limit weakens only marginally from $\sum m_\nu < 0.052$ eV (purely adiabatic) to $< 0.057$ eV (including NDI), with the NDI amplitude consistent with zero. In the CPL dynamical dark energy model, the adiabatic limit is $< 0.111$ eV, shifting to $< 0.115$ eV with NDI, yet the isocurvature mode remains undetected.

canonical_record.label: Hierarchy-aware prior relaxes cosmological mass-sum bound
canonical_record.summary: The 2026 cosmological isocurvature analysis reported that its purely adiabatic ΛCDM upper limit of 0.052 eV lay below the oscillation-implied normal-ordering minimum of 0.05878 eV because of a statistical prior extending to zero, while a hierarchy-informed prior raised the reported upper limit to 0.092 eV.

sources.title: Constraints on the Sum of Neutrino Masses from ACT DR6 and DESI DR2 Considering Isocurvature Initial Conditions

statement: The 2026 cosmological isocurvature analysis reported that its purely adiabatic ΛCDM upper limit of 0.052 eV lay below the oscillation-implied normal-ordering minimum of 0.05878 eV because of a statistical prior extending to zero, while a hierarchy-informed prior raised the reported upper limit to 0.092 eV.

scope.population: Joint CMB-SPA, DESI DR2 BAO and DES Year 5 supernova analysis
scope.time: 2026 paper, comparing alternative neutrino mass-sum priors
scope.assumptions: The 0.052 eV bound is conditional on an unconstrained-from-below-by-oscillation mass prior; the 0.092 eV bound reflects a hierarchy-informed prior.
scope.uncertainty: The paper's prior analysis does not show that the mass sum is physically negative or establish neutrino hierarchy from cosmology.
scope.quantifiers: initial 95% limit 0.052 eV, oscillation floor 0.05878 eV, revised 95% upper limit 0.092 eV

support.quote: Notably, the adiabatic $\Lambda$CDM limit of $0.052$ eV lies below the minimum sum required by the normal neutrino mass hierarchy ($0.05878$ eV), indicating that this bound is an artifact of the statistical prior extending to zero. Imposing a physically motivated hierarchy-informed prior raises the limit to $< 0.092$ eV. Our results demonstrate that current data show no evidence for NDI modes and that the inferred neutrino mass upper limit is robust against this extension, but a definitive, model-independent bound requires addressing prior dependencies and dark energy uncertainties.
